title: 20 Lessons from History's Greatest Persuaders
summary: This content shares twenty historical figures and a core persuasive lesson from each. The main idea is that effective influence comes from understanding others, building trust, and framing ideas around their needs and desires.
key_points: Dale Carnegie: A person's name is the sweetest sound to them, so learn and use it.
Zig Ziglar: You get everything you want by helping enough other people get what they want.
Mary Kay Ash: Treat every person like they are wearing a sign that says, "Make me feel important."
Socrates: Ask good enough questions, and people will talk themselves into the answer.
Aristotle: People decide if they trust you before they decide if you're right.
Robert Cialdini: People say yes to people they like, and they like people who are like them.
Chris Voss: Nobody moves until they feel understood, so say what they're feeling before you say what you want.
Warren Buffett: Price is what you pay; value is what you get.
Sam Walton: There is only one boss, the customer, and they can fire everyone by shopping somewhere else.
Jeff Bezos: Start with what the customer needs and work backwards from there.
Steve Jobs: A lot of people don't know what they want until you show it to them.
David Ogilvy: The customer isn't stupid, so stop talking to them like they are.
Phil Knight: He couldn't sell encyclopedias, but he could sell shoes because he believed in running.
Sun Tzu: The best fight is the one you win without having it.
Abraham Lincoln: If you want to win someone over, first convince them you're their friend.
Muhammad Ali: He called himself the greatest before anyone agreed, and that's part of why they did.
Daniel Kahneman: Losing something hurts about twice as much as winning it feels good.
Estée Lauder: Her best advertising was one happy customer telling a friend.
Martin Luther King Jr.: He said, "I have a dream" not "I have a plan", and people followed the dream.
Theodore Roosevelt: Speak softly and carry a big stick; stay calm and always have another option.
